CONTEXT.content: Shipping code is easy. Shipping safely means you can detect problems fast and roll back without drama.
CONTEXT.analogy: Canary in a coal mine — small exposure detects danger before everyone is affected.
CONTEXT.productionNote: Deploy frequency matters less than mean time to detect and recover.

DECIDE.optionA: Big-bang deploy: all instances at once with health check gate.
DECIDE.optionB: Progressive rollout: 5% → 25% → 100% with metric monitoring between stages.

tradeoffs.A: Simple tooling; blast radius is entire fleet.
tradeoffs.B: Limits damage; needs metrics and orchestration.

hints: What metrics would stop a bad rollout?

BUILD.goal: Document a rollout checklist: pre-deploy checks, deploy steps, metrics to watch, rollback procedure.

tracks.node: Include npm test, health endpoint, error rate threshold.
tracks.typescript: Include bun test, health check, 5xx rate.

acceptance: Rollback steps executable in under 5 minutes
hints: Rollback should be practiced, not theoretical.

criteria: Simulate failed deploy — rollback completes successfully
Metrics thresholds are numeric, not vague
hints: Run a game day: deploy bad code on purpose in staging.

BREAK.scenario: Deploy succeeds but error rate climbs 10 minutes later — memory leak.
BREAK.symptoms: Health check passed at deploy time. Errors correlate with traffic volume.
hints: Why didn't health check catch this?

FIX.goal: Add memory/latency alerts to rollout gate. Update checklist to soak-test before full rollout.
hints: Health at T+0 isn't enough — watch T+15min.

decisionCallbacks.A: Big-bang would have taken down everything before you noticed the leak.
decisionCallbacks.B: Progressive rollout limited blast radius — but needed better post-deploy metrics.
